samples.identification: Saved GitHub blob page for Chris Campbell / obscuresec Shmoocon IX Invoke-TwitterBot source
evidence: HTML parsing finds fourteen script tags: executable loads are GitHub asset scripts; inline bodies are JSON data/import maps. There are no inline event-handler attributes. The complete 947-line PowerShell source is in rawLines JSON and escaped rendered source, not an executable script element or interpreter call.

Independently extracted and traced the entire bot: tweet timeline XML -> status text -> pipe-split dispatch; !run builds cmd.exe /C; !downexec downloads then invokes PowerShell; !upload sends Base64 local-file contents to Pastebin; !credential prompts and logs plaintext credentials; !persist saves a downloaded cache.db and a Startup shortcut.

The source also implements an accepted-socket/cmd stream bridge, keyboard polling with foreground-window attribution and file logging, and LSASS-token duplication/SetThreadToken. These source capabilities remain relevant notable observations on the saved page; their presence does not make the page execute the bot.
Decoded the two Base64 constants independently: one is EICAR, the other is $A = GC $env:ProgramData\cache.db; IEX $A. No additional encoded executable payload was recovered.

Conference attribution, BSD license and engagement-IP/work-hour checks support research context. There is no top-level invocation even in the extracted script; its 2013-02-16 kill date exits before networking today. BindShell/GetSystem/KeyLog switch handlers have mismatched names; propagation is not implemented.
samples.limits: Remote GitHub assets were not executed. A separately extracted, modified or invoked PowerShell implant would require a different deployment assessment. This verdict is about the supplied saved HTML bytes.
samples.changes: No page-specific behavioral rule was weakened or suppressed.

samples.identification: gorvet/gframe PHP framework 4.3.0 with SweetAlert2 11.10.0 and TinyMCE 8.6.0
evidence: Reviewed archive inventory (1734 entries), Composer lifecycle/autoload declarations, asynchronous task execution and workers, browser module deployment, global page metadata and the flagged JavaScript call paths. Ordinary process execution, closure serialization, OpenSSL, HTTP, and editor upload operations fit the framework purpose and retain their detections.

SweetAlert2 top-level factory tests Russian navigator.language and location.host ending .ru/.su/.by/.xn--p1ai. It persists swal-initiation in localStorage; after more than three days it waits 500 ms, assigns document.body.style.pointerEvents="none", appends an audio element using a remote MP3, sets loop=true and calls play after 2500 ms while swallowing playback failures. Pointer blocking precedes and does not depend on successful audio playback.

The routine runs at library load, not only on a user-requested dialog. The default SweetAlert2 module deploys the asset, and skeleton/global.meta.php, install.php, admin/auth/account views and recovery metadata load it into ordinary browser pages.

Module documentation describes normal dialogs and theming, does not disclose regional lockout/audio behavior, and supplies no extension-only or data-only delivery guard. This is an active vendored sabotage routine; no malicious intent is attributed to the framework author.

The listed SweetAlert2 and all three TinyMCE files are byte-identical to their exact upstream npm releases fetched with forager. Upstream origin establishes identity and absence of local changes, not benign behavior. TinyMCE Function("return this;")() is a global-object fallback, XHR sends user-selected image blobs to configured upload settings, and the silver theme stores colors/history and routes dialog messages.
samples.limits: Actual affected users, page hostname/port, language, prior storage timestamp and autoplay policy are unknown. The archive verdict reflects shipped reachable conditional sabotage. No separate TinyMCE malware, credential theft or extra payload was established.
samples.coverage_note: Retained three hostile archive findings and the hostile member routine. They describe a two-effect routine (pointer lockout and forced remote looping audio), its archive bundling, and protestware identity. No duplicate technique was added merely to increase counts.
samples.changes: Preserved both source-name matches while relocating them away from exfiltration/OS privilege claims.

samples.identification: Backdoored SquirrelMail redirect.php login handler, revision 12352
evidence: Before loading dependencies or checking login state, the injected HTTP_BASE_PATH branch defines SM_PATH from a client-set request header. The next literal ../ definition cannot replace an already defined PHP constant.

Nine require_once expressions use the same constant, beginning functions/global.php. A supplied root therefore selects executable PHP dependency paths before authentication. A local attacker-planted path works as file inclusion; remote inclusion additionally depends on PHP URL-include configuration.

The otherwise ordinary SquirrelMail flow gets login credentials, pads/encrypts the password for IMAP login, records session and cookie state, computes the redirect, and parses accepted attachment types. Those operations do not explain a client-selected executable include root.

The preserved normal-looking literal root below the injected definition conceals the effective request override. This code-level alteration tips the judgement; it is not based on the collector filename or a historical feed label.
samples.limits: Deployment PHP settings, prior definitions, reachable attacker-hosted/local files and runtime success are not supplied. The unauthenticated request-to-include path and deceptive override are explicit static evidence.
samples.changes: Both hostile behaviors retained; bind define/require and the duplicate literal definition to the same constant; preserve generic definitions as notable; remove Python-specific ATT&CK mapping.

trait_corrections.reason: A path-shaped name assigned from a superglobal establishes neither an include sink nor attacker control; $_SESSION and source examples demonstrate the overclaim. Matcher, effective types, platforms and exclusions are unchanged.

Original rules could convict unrelated constants, quoted examples, guarded defaults and code with no include. Structural queries now bind constant identity, request origin, ordering and an actual include/require prefix. Suspicious structural atoms plus explicit corroborating legs satisfy the current engine requirement for hostile composites; the two original hostile behavior claims remain. Literal captures require complete uninterpolated constant names and request keys. An include must use the constant directly or as a concatenated path prefix, rather than an unrelated arithmetic expression.

The exact substring occurs inside TinyMCE bodySendMessageChannel. It proves neither a class nor webhook transfer. Matcher/type/platform scope retained; unsupported T1041/B0030 defaults removed on relocation.
licenseKeyManagerLoadError matches without any field or OS privilege operation. Same substring, JS/TS scope and platforms retained.

Updated exact consumers and retained moved observations explicitly in the Discord URL and Apps Script license-context exclusions. Broad positive exfiltration selectors no longer receive a bare name as theft evidence. Destination source-name ancestors have no broad selector consumers.
Broadened the existing neutral php-define-from-superglobal atom to include $_REQUEST, corroborated by a new actual request-to-include positive. No new duplicate definition atom was added.
